methodological_rigor.justification: Post hoc analysis of the phase III KEYNOTE-585 RCT (NCT03221426) leveraging the full ITT population (n=1007) with prospectively collected outcomes. Pathologic endpoints (pCR, mPR via Mandard grade 1-2, pDS) are defined and compared with EFS and OS via Kaplan-Meier and unstratified Cox regression. The analyses are explicitly labeled post hoc and hypothesis-generating; no multiplicity adjustment, no trial-level surrogacy analysis (only patient-level within a single trial), and some subgroup HRs have wide CIs (e.g., mPR EFS HR 0.6 [0.4-1.0]). Baseline imbalance in pathologic nodal N0 (44.0% vs 34.1%) could affect downstream inference.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Secondary post hoc analysis of one RCT (KEYNOTE-585); Oxford LoE for this analysis is 2b (individual cohort within an RCT). Clinical relevance is meaningful because the primary trial did not meet statistical significance for EFS; the pathologic endpoint analysis provides mechanistic support for continued investigation of neoadjuvant ICI in gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma but cannot establish surrogacy from a single trial. Findings inform trial-design discussions rather than immediate practice.

reporting_quality.justification: Secondary analysis of an RCT; CONSORT extensions for post hoc subgroup reporting are applicable, and the original KEYNOTE-585 trial is referenced (Shitara et al., Lancet Oncol 2024). Trial registration (NCT03221426) and data cut-off are specified. Limitations are candidly stated (post hoc, limited subgroup sample sizes, missing MSI status in 15%, no multiplicity adjustment). No data-sharing statement or individual patient data repository described in the normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors position this as the first analysis of pCR/mPR/pDS as survival surrogates specifically for neoadjuvant immunotherapy in locally advanced resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma. Related evidence exists for chemotherapy-only neoadjuvant contexts (Becker, Smyth MRC-MAGIC, Zhu tumor regression grading) and for NSCLC/breast/bladder ICI settings (Hines 2024, KEYNOTE-522). The contribution is contextual rather than mechanistic and is explicitly hypothesis-generating.

writing_presentation.justification: Concise, well-structured post hoc analysis paper with clear baseline table, surrogate outcome table, Kaplan-Meier figures (EFS/OS by pCR/mPR/pDS), and Sankey plots for stage migration. Discussion candidly acknowledges discordance between pCR improvement and non-significant EFS, notes MATTERHORN parallel, and lists limitations. Some bullet summaries are duplicative and Table 1 includes an irrelevant 'PCR' legend entry (polymerase chain reaction) alongside pCR that risks confusion.

key_strengths: Leverages full ITT population (n=1007) of a large phase III RCT with mature follow-up (median 46.3 months)
Multiple clinically relevant surrogate endpoints (pCR, mPR, pDS to N0, any pDS) analyzed against EFS and OS
Numerically consistent improvements in EFS/OS for patients achieving surrogate endpoints, with mPR showing HR trends favoring pembrolizumab arm
Candid acknowledgment of discordance between pCR signal and non-significant EFS in parent trial
key_concerns: Post hoc analysis without multiplicity adjustment; confirmatory surrogacy requires trial-level meta-analysis
Single-trial patient-level analysis cannot establish formal surrogate validity
Missing MSI status in 15% of patients may confound interpretation given known MSI-H sensitivity to ICIs
Baseline imbalance in pathologic N0 (44% vs 34%) between arms may bias within-responder comparisons
No individual-patient-data repository or sharing statement visible
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically straightforward, carefully framed post hoc surrogate-endpoint analysis of KEYNOTE-585 with appropriately modest conclusions; tier 2 with minor revisions reflects the large randomized parent trial and clinical relevance despite inherent post hoc limitations.
